statement: You are given a directed graph with n vertices as an n × n matrix. matrix[i][j] is the weight of the edge from i to j, or −1 when there is no such edge. The distance from a vertex to itself is 0.

Compute the shortest distance between every ordered pair of vertices using the Floyd–Warshall algorithm: for each vertex k in turn, allow paths to pass through k, and replace dist[i][j] with dist[i][k] + dist[k][j] whenever that is shorter.
Return the resulting n × n matrix, keeping −1 for every pair with no path at all.

examples.explanation: There is no direct edge 0 → 2, but 0 → 1 → 2 costs 4 + 1 = 5. Likewise 1 → 2 → 3 gives 1 → 3 a distance of 4. No edge enters vertex 0, so every other row keeps −1 in column 0.
The only new route is 2 → 0 → 1 with length 4 + 3 = 7. Vertex 1 has no outgoing edge, so its row stays −1 except for itself.
